transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Since the divorce I eat huge meals by myself late at night because I’m embarrassed by how much I eat around other people. My sister noticed how I was acting and convinced me that I needed to talk to someone about it.
Do you feel distressed about the nighttime eating, or do you feel like you can't stop eating even when you're not hungry?

Yes, I feel deeply ashamed about it, which is why I hide away in my apartment to do it. Once I start, it's like a switch flips and I just can't stop myself, even when I'm already completely full and not hungry at all.
Do you regularly wake up during the night and eat, or are you starting these large meals while already awake in the evening?

I'm already awake when this happens. It starts right after I get home from work in the evening, when I cook a massive late dinner and eat it in front of the TV. I don't wake up in the middle of the night to eat.
Do you ever eat while partially asleep or have no memory of eating upon waking up?
No, I am completely awake and aware of everything I'm doing. I remember all of it, and I definitely don't eat while I'm asleep.
Do you ever feel a loss of control during these evening eating episodes, like you’re unable to stop eating or control how much you eat?
Yes, absolutely. Once I start, it's like a switch flips and I'm just shoveling food in. Even while I'm telling myself to stop, my hands keep going back to the pot like they're not listening to me.
Do these episodes happen almost every night, or only a few times a week?

It doesn't happen every single night, but it is at least a few nights every week. On those nights, I come home, cook a massive late dinner just for myself, and end up binging in front of the TV until I can't even move.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was F50.8 (Other specified eating disorder), and it remains the most appropriate code based on the current information. The patient exhibits recurrent episodes of binge eating in the evening while fully awake, with a clear sense of loss of control, associated distress, and functional impairment (eating alone due to embarrassment, shame). These episodes occur while awake, ruling out sleep-related eating disorders (e.g., Nocturnal Eating Syndrome, which would be coded under F51.8). The pattern does not align with night eating syndrome (which involves morning anorexia, evening hyperphagia, and nocturnal awakenings with ingestion), as the patient is not eating during sleep or upon involuntary awakenings. The presentation is best characterized as an atypical binge eating disorder variant occurring predominantly in the evening, not meeting full criteria for bulimia nervosa (no compensatory behaviors reported) or BED if frequency/severity thresholds are not met. Thus, F50.8 remains the most accurate classification.
